name: news-20260711-neo4j-rdf-vs-property-graph

summary: A write-up of Neo4j's Jim Webber on 'RDF vs property graphs' (2024) — a knowledge graph's entities, relationships, and organizing principle; the limits of RDF triples and the semantic web (relationships not first-class, SPARQL termination, ontology upkeep); the property graph's advantages with the NASA, Basecamp, and Novo Nordisk cases; ISO GQL; and the conclusion "property graph by default + an ontology layer when needed".

name: news-20260716-kimi-k3
title: Kimi K3 — a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model reaches the frontier
summary: A web-search cross-checked roundup of Moonshot AI's Kimi K3 launch (2.8T total with ~50B active MoE, KDA and AttnRes) — benchmarks such as 3rd on the AA index and 1st in Frontend Arena, $3/$15 pricing, long-horizon autonomous demos like chip design and gravitational-wave analysis, and the self-reported vs independently reproduced gap alongside cyber risk and market fallout.

name: news-20260724-snucatch-ai-coding
title: The End of Coding by Hand? — The Future of Developers as Seen by SNU's Prof. Jaewook Lee
summary: A write-up of the SNU Catch Season 2 talk with Prof. Jaewook Lee (SNU Computer Science and Engineering, director of the AI Institute) plus web cross-checking — the argument that implementation is nearly 100% automated while problem definition and critique remain, the power of vibe coding and the 95% trap, the education problem of students becoming couriers and an AI-native curriculum, the lessons of the Jevons paradox and bank tellers after the ATM, and entry-level developer employment at -20% (Stanford/ADP) alongside METR's measured 19%.

name: news-20260724-claude-opus-5
title: Claude Opus 5 — A Near-Fable at Half the Price Has Arrived
summary: A cross-verified account of Anthropic's 2026-07-24 Claude Opus 5 launch from the official announcement and multiple press reports — at $5/$25 it lands within 0.5% of Fable 5's CursorBench 3.2 max peak at half the cost per task, with Frontier-Bench 43.3%, OSWorld 2.0 on ⅓ the budget and 3× on ARC-AGI 3, a long-horizon agentic demo that wrote its own CV pipeline to rebuild FreeCAD 3D when it could not view the drawing, plus the context of the Fable 5 safeguard false-positive controversy and a separation of unconfirmed claims

name: news-20260709-ai-2040-plan-a

summary: The overview and hub of a commentary series on the follow-up normative scenario from the authors of AI 2027 (AI Futures Project) — a recommendation rather than a prediction, covering the core idea of delaying superintelligence to 2040 through a US-China agreement, the one-line gist, an interactive timeline and a comparison with AI 2027, and pointing to the three installments on the scenario, the policy and the reactions

name: news-20260709-ai-2040-scenario
title: AI 2040: Plan A — the year-by-year scenario (2027 → 2040)
summary: The world Plan A paints year by year — 2027 two workforces (humans + AI agents), 2028 the election and data center costs, 2029 the US-China agreement, 2030 averting full automation, 2030-35 expansion to expert level, 2035 a pause to keep control, 2040 the release and superintelligence, stated explicitly as a recommendation rather than a prediction

name: news-20260709-ai-2040-policy
title: AI 2040: Plan A — Policy and Verification
summary: The mechanisms that hold the deal together — total research transparency, the verification protocol (network taps and partial recomputation), SL5 security, relocated data centers (US to Mongolia, China to Canada), mutually assured compute destruction, the model spec and third-party oversight; the original's interactive Supplements explorer is carried here only as a static summary

name: news-20260709-ai-2040-reactions
title: AI 2040: Plan A — Reactions and Critiques
summary: A board of support and criticism after the release. Richard Ngo's three objections (the ambiguity of an optimistic forecast, the 2040 handover of power, the politics of optimism, published alongside at the authors' request), Dave Friedman (technical legibility is not political feasibility), Rohit Krishnan (underspecified terms), plus coverage from Scott Alexander, WaPo and Axios
